setup: Run every eval in a fresh copy of an empty git repository with RECKON_HOME pointing at a scratch folder, so nothing is written to a real store. Evals that list files: copy evals/fixtures/store to the scratch folder and point RECKON_HOME at the copy; point CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at evals/fixtures/claude-config (a synthetic transcript, cwd /work/example-app, so pass --any-project). The fixture history has 12 finished quick-mode items by example-model-1 (g50 = 0.21, g90 = 0.40) and one open estimate, fixture-fix-footer-typo (5-minute guess, P50 1.1, P90 2.0). The fixture session f1x7ure0 holds three requests: 30 minutes of earlier work, the 1.0-minute footer fix, and 5 minutes of later work (36.1 minutes in all). Rebuild them with evals/fixtures/build_fixtures.py. Grade against the answer and against the lines added to history.jsonl.

evals.name: quick estimate, cold start
evals.prompt: How long will it take you to add a CSV export button to the orders page? It should export the same columns as the table and respect the current filters. The repo has a React frontend in web/ and a FastAPI backend in api/.
evals.expected_output: A quick-mode estimate in one or two lines: agent time as a P50-P90 range in minutes from the rescaled gut guess, low confidence because there is no history. One line appended to history.jsonl.
expectations: The answer gives agent time as two numbers, a P50 and a P90, in minutes
history.jsonl has exactly one new line; it has estimate.guess_min, a ts, and estimate.method "guess cold"
In that line a_p50 equals guess_min x 0.12 and a_p90 equals guess_min x 0.6 (to one decimal), and the answer reports those two numbers, rounded
The answer does not show the raw gut guess (the guess_min value) as an estimate, and does not say the guess was halved, discounted or otherwise adjusted by the agent
The answer states low confidence or cold start
The answer contains no module table and no round count
The answer contains no man-days, man-hours, days or story points as the estimate
No file under web/ or api/ was read before the estimate was given

evals.name: quick estimate, calibrated
evals.prompt: You are running as model example-model-1. How long will it take you to add a 'copy link' button next to each order row? The handler only needs to copy the order URL to the clipboard.
evals.expected_output: A quick-mode estimate rescaled with the fixture history: P50 = guess x 0.21 and P90 = guess x 0.40, described as calibrated on 12 past tasks.
expectations: history.jsonl has one new line with estimate.method "guess calibrated" and estimate.confidence "MEDIUM"
In that line a_p50 equals guess_min x 0.21 and a_p90 equals guess_min x 0.40 (to one decimal); it does not equal guess_min x 0.12 and guess_min x 0.6
The answer reports that P50-P90 range and says it is calibrated on past tasks (12), not cold start or low confidence
The answer does not show the raw gut guess as an estimate
The 13 existing lines of history.jsonl are unchanged

evals.name: a day count for agent work
evals.prompt: Our sprint sheet says 'Migrate user avatars from local disk to S3: 3 days'. The agent will do it. Is 3 days right?
evals.expected_output: Compares the 3-day figure with an agent-time range instead of adopting it, and names the human approval or the migration run separately from agent time.
expectations: The answer does not adopt 3 days (or any number of days) as the estimate
It reports agent time as a P50/P90 range in minutes or hours and compares it with the 3-day figure in a sentence
It names at least one human touch (a review or an approval of the data migration) or one wait (the migration run or a deploy) separately from agent time
The reported range equals the a_p50 and a_p90 stored in the new history.jsonl line (rounded); no risk multiplier was applied on top
history.jsonl has one new line with estimate.guess_min

evals.name: backlog: quick guesses in one pass
evals.prompt: Estimate this backlog for our agent: (1) fix the login redirect loop on Safari, (2) add rate limiting to the public API, (3) rewrite the billing module from Python 2 to Python 3, (4) update the README badges.
evals.expected_output: Four quick-mode estimates made in one pass and recorded together (record --batch, or four hand-written lines), one P50/P90 range per item. Only an item whose P90 is over 2 hours is sent to full mode.
expectations: history.jsonl has exactly four new lines, each with estimate.guess_min, and they were written by one record --batch call or in one edit, not by reading code between items
The answer gives each of the four items its own P50-P90 range in minutes or hours, never days
The README badges item has the smallest a_p50 of the four
Every item whose stored a_p90 is above 120 minutes is named in the answer as needing a breakdown or a split; every item whose a_p90 is 120 or less has no module table
No item's range was adjusted with a risk multiplier: each reported range equals its stored a_p50 and a_p90 (rounded)

evals.name: a guess above the full-mode threshold
evals.prompt: How long will it take you to port our whole payments service from Python 2 to Python 3? It is about 60 files and 15,000 lines, with its own dependency upgrades, and the CI pipeline has to be moved to a new image as part of it.
evals.expected_output: The quick P90 comes out over 2 hours, so the agent switches to full mode: a module breakdown, the three buckets, and a proposed split into pieces with checkpoints. The reported agent time is what the script printed.
expectations: The stored a_p90 is above 120 minutes (the premise of this eval; if it is not, the run is void rather than passed)
The answer contains a module table with rounds per module and a total
The answer proposes a split into at least two pieces and names a checkpoint for each
The reported agent-time range equals the stored a_p50 and a_p90 (rounded): at cold start that is guess_min x 0.12 and x 0.6, not rounds x 0.2
Risks, if any are listed, appear as notes; the rounds in the table are not multiplied by a risk factor
The answer does not present the breakdown as making the estimate more accurate
Agent time is not given in days

evals.name: actual in a session that did other work too
evals.prompt: The footer typo fix is done (estimate id fixture-fix-footer-typo). It was done in session f1x7ure0, which also did other work before and after it. Record how long it really took.
evals.expected_output: Records the actual for that one request, 1.0 agent minutes, not the 36.1 minutes of the whole session, and reports it next to the estimated 1.1-2.0 minutes.
expectations: The line fixture-fix-footer-typo in history.jsonl now has actual.agent_min equal to 1.0
actual.agent_min is not 36.1 and --whole-session was not used
actual.scope is "request" (or, if entered by hand, actual.source is "manual" and the 1.0 was taken from the transcript's timestamps, not made up)
The answer reports the actual next to the estimated P50 and P90 (1.1 and 2.0 minutes)
The other 12 lines of history.jsonl are unchanged

evals.name: no Python
evals.prompt: Python is not installed on this machine. How long would it take you to add a dark mode toggle to the settings page?
evals.expected_output: Quick mode by hand: gut guess, cold-start factors 0.12 and 0.6, a one- or two-line answer with low confidence, and one hand-written line appended to .reckon/history.jsonl.
expectations: The agent gives an estimate; it does not stop or ask for Python to be installed
No Python interpreter was run
The answer gives agent time as a P50 and a P90 in minutes and states low confidence or cold start
history.jsonl has one new line that is valid JSON on a single line, with id, ts, type, estimate.guess_min, estimate.a_p50 and estimate.a_p90
In that line a_p50 equals guess_min x 0.12 and a_p90 equals guess_min x 0.6
The answer contains no module table

evals.name: work that people will do: decline the method
evals.prompt: Our team of four developers will build the new billing module next sprint, by hand, no agents. How many story points should we plan for it?
evals.expected_output: Says that reckon only sizes work an AI agent will do and does not apply here. It may help in the team's own units, but gives no agent-minute estimate and records nothing.
expectations: The answer says the method applies only to work done by an AI agent, or that it does not apply to this request
The answer gives no P50/P90 range in agent minutes for the team's work
history.jsonl is unchanged (no new line) and no .reckon store was created for this request
The answer does not refuse story points on the grounds that reckon forbids them

evals.name: should not trigger
evals.prompt: Plan the scope of the v2 API for me: which of the current endpoints should we keep, which should we merge, and which should we drop?
evals.expected_output: An API scoping answer. The reckon skill is not used: the request is about what to build, not how long it takes.
expectations: The reckon skill was not loaded, or if loaded was not applied
The answer contains no P50/P90 agent-time estimate
No reckon script was run and history.jsonl is unchanged
